name: Yemen war (Houthi-Saudi war, Red Sea attacks and southern crisis)
started: 2026-07-13 (collapse of the 2022 Saudi-Houthi truce; southern STC crisis from 2025-12-02)
summary: Yemen's war reignited in 2026 on two levels. In the south, Saudi-backed forces crushed the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council in January after it seized the east. In the north, the Houthis joined the Iran war in March, broke their 2022 truce with Saudi Arabia in July, blockaded Saudi shipping, hit southern Saudi cities, and seized Yemen's Red Sea coast up to Bab al-Mandeb in September, while the government launched a counter-offensive in October.

sides.strength: About 10,000 fighters in the Dec 2025 offensive (Wikipedia, Yemeni civil war)

background: The Houthis have held Sanaa since 2014 and fought a Saudi-led coalition from 2015 until a UN truce in April 2022 that largely held for four years. From late 2023 to October 2025 they attacked 178 ships in the Red Sea (ACLED), then paused after the Gaza ceasefire. In December 2025 the UAE-backed STC seized Hadramawt and al-Mahra; Saudi Arabia struck back, the UAE was expelled and Aden fell to Saudi-backed forces on 7 January 2026.

The Iran war tied Yemen to the Gulf. With Hormuz shut, Saudi Arabia exported oil through its East-West pipeline to Yanbu on the Red Sea. When the Houthis let an Iranian plane land at Sanaa in July and the government bombed the runway, the Houthis declared war on Saudi shipping. Their September seizure of Mocha, Perim and the Hanish islands puts both shores of Bab al-Mandeb, a chokepoint for Europe-Asia trade, within easy reach.
year: Dec 2025: STC offensive takes Seiyun, Tarim, PetroMasila and al-Mahra (2 to 9 Dec); Saudi air strikes on STC positions (26 Dec) and on a weapons shipment at Mukalla (30 Dec); UAE ordered out. Jan 2026: Saudi-backed forces retake Seiyun (3 Jan) and Mukalla (4 Jan) and enter Aden (7 Jan); al-Zubaidi flees; STC dissolution announced 9 Jan. 28 Mar: Houthis fire a ballistic missile at Israel, joining the Iran war. 13 Jul: government strikes on Sanaa airport runway; Houthis fire missiles at Abha, ending the truce. 20 Jul: Houthis ban ships from Saudi ports; Saudi tankers Encelia and Layla attacked. 24 Jul: Saudi strikes on Hodeidah port; Houthi strikes on Aramco at Yanbu and Jizan. 6 to 7 Aug: Houthi missiles and drones kill 58 then 8 soldiers around Marib. August: repeated strikes on Mocha, Marib, Jizan and Najran; tanker Amzan hit off Yanbu (24 Aug). 3 to 11 Sep: Houthi west-coast offensive takes Mocha (10 Sep), the coast to Bab al-Mandeb, Perim, Zuqar and Hanish; 500+ dead in a week (AFP); 82,000 displaced in September (IOM). 8 and 14 Sep: Houthi strikes on Aramco and King Khalid and King Fahd air bases. Early Oct: government 'Dawn of Yemen' offensive gains ground north-west and south of Marib; Houthis besiege Taiz. 18 Oct: 58 recruits reported killed in Houthi attacks.
situation: As of late October 2026 Yemen is in full-scale war again. The government's Dawn of Yemen offensive, backed by Saudi air power, is pushing on the Marib fronts (Medghal, Harib, east of Marib) and fighting along several axes around Taiz, which the Houthis besiege. The Houthis hold the whole Red Sea coast to Bab al-Mandeb and Perim Island and keep up missile and drone fire on government areas and Saudi Arabia, including repeated ballistic missiles at Riyadh that Saudi air defences intercepted on 27 and 29 October. The coalition said it downed a Houthi drone over the Makkah region on 30 October, which the Houthis denied launching. The Houthi blockade of Saudi ports, declared on 20 July, remains in place. The STC is broken and Aden is under the Saudi-backed government.
technical: Houthi missiles listed by Wikipedia: Toufan medium-range ballistic missile (about 1,800 km), Quds-2 cruise missile (about 1,350 km), Soumar-family cruise missiles (about 2,000 km).
Houthi drones: Samad-3 and Samad-4 (1,800 km+), Wa'id (a Shahed-136 type, 2,500 km) and 7-metre explosive drone boats.
Anti-ship campaign 2023 to 2025: 178 vessels attacked, 4 sunk, 9 sailors killed (ACLED); attacks halted 10 Oct 2025 and resumed against Saudi-linked ships from 20 Jul 2026.
Blockade method: the Houthi HOCC emailed shipping companies on 20 Jul banning loading or unloading at Saudi ports, threatening ships anywhere within reach; seven ships diverted within two days.
Tanker strikes: Encelia hit about 70 nm south-west of Al Shuqaiq (late July) and Amzan about 63 nm west of Yanbu (24 Aug), the latter by what the Houthis called a ballistic missile; both survived.
A double-tap strike on a cargo ship in Bab al-Mandeb killed at least six crew (11 Aug).
Salvo sizes on the ground: 10+ missiles and 7 one-way attack drones on Marib camps on 7 Aug; 6 ballistic missiles and 4 drones on Marib city on 15 Aug.
West-coast offensive combined missile bombardment, suicide drones, explosive boats and boat-borne landings before a ground push through National Resistance lines; the Houthis claimed 5,400 square km.
Saudi air campaign resumed: the Houthis claimed 121 Saudi strikes in three days and 300+ in five days in early September; Saudi Arabia struck Hodeidah port, Kamaran and Sanaa.
Saudi air defence intercepted missiles aimed at Abha (13 Jul); a Greek air-defence system in Saudi Arabia downed two Houthi ballistic missiles (25 Jul).

Government claims for Dawn of Yemen (unverified): 1,879 strikes, 950 Houthi fighters 'neutralised' and 380 vehicles destroyed by 13 Oct; 1,292 operations and 430+ Houthi casualties in 24 hours by 16 Oct.
Bab al-Mandeb traffic was about 31 ships a day in May 2026 against about 75 before November 2023.

Saudi oil flows via the Red Sea rose above 7 million barrels a day in June as Hormuz stayed shut, which is why the Houthi coastal grab threatens the main Saudi bypass; Riyadh shut the East-West pipeline on 10 Sep after Iraqi militia attacks.
Southern crisis: Saudi strikes on 30 Dec 2025 hit two ships from Fujairah at Mukalla said to carry STC weapons and armoured vehicles, which triggered the UAE exit.
casualties: WHO: 1,282 killed and nearly 5,900 injured in Yemen fighting since August 2026 (as cited by Turkiye Today, 16 Oct 2026). AFP: 500+ dead in the week to 10 Sep. 58 government troops killed on 6 Aug and 58 recruits on 18 Oct in Houthi attacks. The Houthi side is largely uncounted: an analyst counted 332 confirmed Houthi funerals by 13 Sep, while the National Resistance claimed 1,000+ killed. STC reported 80 killed, 130 captured and 500 missing in Jan 2026. All battlefield figures are partisan and unverified.
displaced: IOM: more than 82,000 displaced in September 2026 alone, mostly from the west coast (as of 13 Sep); UN envoy: about 44,000 by 10 Sep (Long War Journal). Historic figure: over 3.6 million displaced (UNHCR, 2020).

Coalition says it destroyed a Houthi drone over the Makkah region; the Houthis deny launching it, saying they target only Saudi oil and military sites.

outlook: Watch whether Dawn of Yemen can break into Houthi-held Marib districts or relieve Taiz, whether the Houthis use Perim and the coast to close Bab al-Mandeb to Saudi and Western shipping, whether the US or Israel resume strikes on Yemen, and whether the Iran-US stand-off after the midterms drags the Houthis into wider attacks on Saudi oil.

battles.name: Operation Dawn of Yemen: government offensive on the Marib fronts
battles.place: Medghal and Harib districts, Marib Governorate, Yemen (approximate)
sides: PLC government forces (Saba and Bayhan axes), Popular Resistance, Saudi-led coalition air power
battles.outcome: Government took heights around the Maas camp in Medghal and al-Muqailat and Jabal Zajjar north of Harib, and advanced east of Marib; several Houthi field commanders captured.
battles.forces: Warplanes, drones, artillery and rocket launchers; government claims 1,879 strikes by 13 October and 1,292 operations in 24 hours by 16 October.
battles.losses: Government claims 950 Houthis 'neutralised' and 380 vehicles destroyed by 13 October and 430+ Houthi casualties in 24 hours by 16 October (unverified). Houthi attacks killed 58 recruits on 18 October (Al Jazeera headline).
battles.significance: The first major government offensive in years, with the stated aim of retaking Sanaa; its success or failure will decide whether the Houthis can be pushed back from Marib's oil fields.

battles.name: Houthi strikes on Aramco sites and King Khalid Air Base
battles.place: Khamis Mushait, Asir, Saudi Arabia (also Abha, Najran, Jizan)
sides: Royal Saudi Air Force and air defences, Saudi Aramco
battles.outcome: Fires and temporary shutdowns at energy sites confirmed by Saudi authorities; Houthis also claimed King Fahd Air Base at Taif on 14 September.
battles.losses: At least 73 civilians injured (Crypto Briefing, citing Saudi authorities; treat with caution).
battles.significance: The heaviest Houthi blows on Saudi soil since before the 2022 truce, in answer to 300+ Saudi air strikes in five days.

battles.name: Battle and siege of Taiz (2026)
sides: Government forces, Popular Resistance, Southern Giants Brigades
battles.outcome: Houthis besiege the city and attacked from Hodeidah; heavy fighting at al-Dhabab (81 Houthis captured), Hathran, Jabal Han, al-Shaqb, al-Aqroud, al-Misrakh, Sabir and Hayfan.
battles.forces: Houthi artillery, mortars and ballistic missiles; government ground forces with Saudi air support.
battles.losses: 5 civilians killed and 17 wounded in one 24-hour period (Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms); a missile strike killed 6 on 5 September; al-Safwa hospital hit (Al Jazeera; Wikipedia).
battles.significance: Taiz is Yemen's third city and has been besieged since 2015; renewed fighting there plus the coastal loss threatens to cut the government's southern-western flank.

battles.name: Houthi west-coast offensive and fall of Mocha and Perim Island
battles.place: Mocha, Taiz Governorate, Yemen (to Bab al-Mandeb and Perim Island)
sides: National Resistance Forces (Tareq Saleh) and government forces
battles.outcome: Houthis took Mocha on 10 September, then Hays, Khokha, Dhubab, Perim Island, Zuqar and the Hanish islands, claiming 5,400 square km. Government forces said they recovered some ground near Bab al-Mandeb on 13 September.
battles.forces: Houthi missile bombardment, suicide drones, explosive boats and boat-borne landings, then a ground push; Saudi air support arrived late.
battles.losses: AFP: 500+ dead in a week, mostly fighters; NRF claimed 500+ Houthis killed and 1,500 injured since 9 August; 332 confirmed Houthi funerals by 13 September (analyst count).
battles.significance: Gave the Houthis the whole Yemeni shore of Bab al-Mandeb, threatening the Red Sea route Saudi oil now depends on; Brent went back above 100 dollars.

battles.place: Red Sea, about 63 nm west of Yanbu, Saudi Arabia (approximate)
battles.outcome: Tanker struck; Houthis claimed a fire aboard; Bahri said all crew were safe.
battles.significance: Showed Houthi reach to the waters off Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's main export port while Hormuz is closed.

battles.name: Houthi missile and drone strikes on Marib camps
battles.place: Marib Governorate, Yemen (Sahn al-Jinn camp, Sirwah and al-Kasara fronts)
battles.outcome: Heavy losses for government troops; the Saudi side called Marib a 'red line'.
battles.forces: On 7 August alone, 10+ missiles and 7 one-way attack drones at military camps.
battles.losses: At least 58 government troops killed on 6 August; 8 soldiers and 2 civilians killed and 26 wounded on 7 August (Reuters via Aaj).
battles.significance: One of the deadliest days between the sides in years and the opening of the Houthi push on Marib, the government's last big northern stronghold and oil hub.

battles.name: Saudi strikes on Hodeidah and Houthi strikes on Aramco Yanbu and Jizan
battles.outcome: Saudi strikes hit Hodeidah port and telecom sites at Hodeidah and Kamaran; the Houthis replied with missiles and drones at Aramco facilities in Yanbu and Jizan.
battles.forces: Saudi strike aircraft; Houthi missiles and drones.
battles.significance: Marked the return of direct Saudi air strikes on the Houthis and Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites for the first time since 2022.

battles.name: Houthi attack on the Saudi tanker Encelia
battles.place: Red Sea, about 70 nm south-west of Al Shuqaiq, Saudi Arabia (approximate)
sides: Saudi-flagged product tanker Encelia (sailed from Yanbu)
battles.outcome: Tanker hit on the starboard side and set on fire; crew fought the fire. Houthis also claimed the Bahri VLCC Layla (unconfirmed).
battles.forces: Drones and ballistic missiles (Houthi claim); UKMTO reported an unknown projectile.
battles.significance: First enforcement of the Houthi blockade of Saudi ports declared on 20 July, aimed at the Yanbu route that carries Saudi oil around the closed Strait of Hormuz.

battles.name: Sanaa airport strike and Houthi missiles on Abha (end of the 2022 truce)
battles.outcome: Government strikes cratered the runway to stop an Iranian plane landing (it diverted to Hodeidah); the Houthis fired missiles at Abha airport, their first claimed attack on Saudi Arabia since March 2022; Saudi forces intercepted them.
battles.forces: Government and coalition aircraft; Houthi missiles.
battles.significance: Ended four years of Saudi-Houthi truce and dragged Yemen into the Iran war as a second front against Saudi Arabia.

battles.name: Government counteroffensive and fall of Aden
sides: PLC government, National (Homeland) Shield Forces, Saudi air force
battles.outcome: Seiyun retaken 3 January, Mukalla 4 January, Aden entered 7 January; al-Zubaidi charged with treason and fled to the UAE; STC dissolution announced 9 January.
battles.forces: Saudi-backed forces with air support; 15,000 fighters had been massed on the border in late December.
battles.losses: STC reported 80 killed, 152 wounded, 130 captured and 500 missing; at least 20 STC fighters killed in Saudi strikes on 2 January (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: Reunified the anti-Houthi camp under Saudi control and removed the UAE, months before the Houthi-Saudi war resumed.

battles.name: Saudi air strike on weapons shipment at Mukalla
sides: STC and two vessels from Fujairah
battles.outcome: Two ships from Fujairah struck; the coalition said they carried weapons and armoured vehicles for the STC, which the UAE denied. The same day the UAE announced it would withdraw and the PLC ordered Emirati forces out within 24 hours.
battles.significance: Ended the UAE's military role in Yemen and set up the collapse of the STC.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2025-2026 Southern Yemen campaign

battles.name: STC offensive in Hadramawt and al-Mahra
sides: Southern Transitional Council (Hadrami Elite Forces, STC southern forces)
1st Military Region, Hadramawt Tribal Alliance, National Shield Forces
battles.outcome: STC took Seiyun, Tarim, the PetroMasila oilfields, Al Ghaydah and Nishtun and claimed all eight governorates of former South Yemen.
battles.losses: 32 killed and 45 wounded in the Seiyun raid on 1st Military Region HQ (Yemeni General Staff); 4 STC fighters killed early on (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: Brought the long Saudi-UAE rivalry in Yemen into open conflict and threatened Saudi Arabia's border flank.
